rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation is in instance_norm_forward_kernel (non-affine). ModelNew uses InstanceNorm2dCustom with affine=True (default). In CUDA code: weight.defined() && bias.defined() == true, so instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine is called. The _with_affine kernel has shared_sq_sum[256] which is NOT mutated.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation modifies shared_sq_sum array size from 256 to 255 in the non-affine kernel (instance_norm_forward_kernel). However, ModelNew instantiates InstanceNorm2dCustom with the default affine=True parameter, which initializes weight and bias as nn.Parameters. When instance_norm_forward_cuda is called, the condition (weight.defined() && bias.defined()) evaluates to true, causing the code to execute instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine instead of the mutated kernel. The affine kernel's shared_sq_sum remains at size 256 and is unaffected by this mutation. Changing the affine parameter would require modifying model configuration, not input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed configuration. The only way to reach the mutated code path would be to instantiate the model with affine=False, which changes the model configuration and violates the testing contract that only allows varying input tensor values.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing GPU kernels, ensure mutations target code paths that are actually reachable under the test configuration. Consider adding separate test cases for each kernel variant (affine vs non-affine) to ensure both paths have coverage.
